escena: SCENE photographed in the Efeonce digital studio, hard neutral daylight raking in from a low window at frame left, physically motivated light with crisp small shadows, no amber cast, modern digital tools. The upper 38 percent is an unbroken smooth graphite plaster wall in deep shadow for white advertising typography to be composed later, no beams, objects or figures in that area. All action is concentrated between 42 and 78 percent of frame height, large enough to understand on a phone. Only one small Codex figure, exact proportions and silhouette of its reference, photographed as a real tactile physical 25cm object, with contact shadows. No people. No paper, no books, no coffee mugs, no company wordmarks, no fabricated logos, no legible screen text. Blue comes from the navy equipment and the figurine, orange is a single physical functional detail, never a global filter. No holograms. Precise real optical texture, sophisticated commercial photography, not CGI. An empty navy swivel chair has just been pushed back diagonally from a digital workbench, a braided cable still unplugged beside a sleeping laptop: the trace of a person who just left. The Codex figure remains alert at the workbench, leaning toward a single landscape tablet propped low on a machined aluminium stand. The screen has a restrained luminous empty rectangular answer space surrounded by tiny abstract neutral rows, no letters. Its little hand points to that empty space, not to the viewer. The missing answer is the visual subject. One tiny orange standby indicator on the aluminium stand. Low seated eye-level, 50mm lens f/2.8. No printed sheets. The tablet stand is anodised active blue #0375DB metal, clearly visible as a functional blue object independently of the mascot, never a background panel.
